 5 Ballot Initiative Election Results You May Have Missed in 2026
 If you’ve only seen the headlines, you may be missing some important state-level ballot initiative results. Here are 5 results that are also important for Americans, especially those in states where these ballot initiatives took place. 
 Published: Nov 10, 2026 
 Kenny Colston 
 Related Issues
 Voting & Fair Representation: Protecting Your Voice 
 x 
 facebook 
 email 
 The results from the 2026 election have been filling headlines, as many states saw complete flips of partisan control, Congress swung heavily, and Americans spoke clearly about control of government. 
 But if you’ve only seen the headlines, you may be missing some important state-level ballot initiative results. Here are 5 results that are also important for Americans, especially those in states where these ballot initiatives took place.  
 1. Election Day Voter Registration Passes in Massachusetts! 
 While this may be a surprise to folks outside of Massachusetts, previously , the Bay State did not allow for voter registration closer than 10 days before an election.    
 But after Common Cause and our allies got Question 4 on the ballot, allowing Election Day registration, Massachusetts voters approved the new measure . Future Massachusetts voters will be able to register on Election Day if they need to, and be able to vote in that election!  
 2. Bad voter bills defeated in Arizona, Colorado and California 
 Unable to hurt voters with a presidential executive order or the terrible SAVE Act or any of its copycats in Congress, groups who support making it harder for eligible voters to cast their ballot went to Arizona, Colorado and California to try and force their agenda through.    
 In all three states, voters rejected restrictive ID measures that would have made it very difficult for voters, especially those who vote by mail, to cast a ballot.    
 Arizona voters saw through a legislative-referred measure that would have made voting harder for a state that has safely relied on mail-in voting for decades. Prop 144 was defeated.     
 Colorado voters saw through millions in dark money funding that would have put their sensitive data at risk on mail-in ballots, rejecting Amendment 84 easily .    
 California voters overwhelmingly rejected putting sensitive info on mail-in ballots and affirmed the current voting system that is safe and secure. 
 3. Campaign finance measure passes in Michigan, convention defeated 
 In Michigan, voters took two pro-democracy steps. They rejected Prop 1, calling for an unwise Article V constitutional convention. And in Prop 2, they approved new campaign finance rules that allow Michiganders to take back power with their elected officials, rather than that power  going to those who can donate the most.   
 4. New Mexico joins rest of the United States, adds legislator pay 
   Before this election, New Mexico state legislators were not paid for their time representing their communities, meaning only those with flexible employment or independent wealth could feel comfortable running for the state legislature.   
 Now, voters have approved New Mexico joining the other 49 states and giving state legislators pay, allowing for those of all incomes to feel comfortable running to represent their communities.    
 5. Missouri rejects badly gerrymandered map 
 In Missouri, voters put the final nail in the coffin for President Donald Trump’s attempt to gerrymander Missouri in a way that reduced Black and brown voices in the state.    
 Trump’s map, already rejected by the courts, was firmly rejected by voters as well.
